name: South Carolina

agency.name: South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation

rates2026.note: No state minimum wage law; federal FLSA rate applies

minWage.smallEmployer: No state minimum wage law: the federal $7.25 applies to employers covered by the FLSA.

tipped.note: Federal FLSA rules ($2.13 cash wage, tipped = more than $30/month).

source.quote: No state minimum wage. Employers subject to the Fair Labor Standards Act must pay the current federal minimum wage of $7.25 per hour.

overtime.note: No state overtime law; federal FLSA applies.

sickLeave.note: No statewide paid sick leave law for private employers.

finalPay.fired: within 48 hours of separation or by the next regular payday, which may not exceed 30 days
finalPay.quit: same rule (applies to separation for any reason)
finalPay.ptoNote: Vacation, holiday and sick pay count as wages only when due under the employer's policy or employment contract.

source.quote: the employer shall pay all wages due to the employee within forty-eight hours of the time of separation or the next regular payday which may not exceed thirty days.

ptoSource.quote: includes vacation, holiday, and sick leave payments which are due to an employee under any employer policy or employment contract.

rightToWorkSource.quote: the right of persons to work must not be denied or abridged because of membership or nonmembership in a labor union or labor organization.

notes.text: Employers who fail to pay wages due can owe three times the unpaid wages plus attorney's fees in a civil action.

source.quote: the employee may recover in a civil action an amount equal to three times the full amount of the unpaid wages, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees

notes.text: Employers must tell each employee in writing at hiring the normal hours, wages, time and place of payment and deductions; changes need 7 days' written notice.

source.quote: Any changes in these terms must be made in writing at least seven calendar days before they become effective.

uncertain: The SC LLR labor pages could not be reached (old URLs 404, site timed out); 'no state minimum wage' relies on the dol.gov state table (cross-check source, updated 2026-07-01). No SC meal/rest break law: SC has no entry in the dol.gov meal-period table.
